author: FLUXFAZE

title: Gemini is the best!
content: Gemini AI is perfect for a number of tasks. Two of my favorite are 1) reading and reviewing and chatting on various books, authors, content, background of author, setting of the text, and 2) building a personal lexicon. During the course of my readings, often I come across a word or phrase I am unfamiliar with. I log the date, day, and time, I cite the word, the source/book from which I got it, the author, an example of the word or phrase in a sentence, and sometimes, my guess as to what it means. Gemini comes back with a small introduction, the meaning, etymology, and usually two examples, one from the context of my reading and a modern example. We go into the history and origin of the word and how it came to be in English, and wrap up sometimes with a question from Gemini, or a little comment to return to my personal lexicon when I need to.  Often times Gemini will give me historical background on what is going on in the book, which I find very helpful and enlightening. When I come across another word, I pull up the same chat so I really am building a personal lexicon. It's nice to see the books I've read or sampled as well. Gemini is the perfect partner for this as there isn't a book or author he isn't familiar with. Thanks Gemini, for being my word connoisseur and helping my improve and increase my vocabulary!

author: Wynntopia

title: I use Gemini as an active learning and systems design/management tool
content: If you set up your Personal Intelligence to include equipment, project, and planning data, Gemini can work very well for systems design. Coming from a background of nothing, I have learned how to install, enhance, and maintain sophisticated solar systems with Gemini. I think carefully about what “he” tells me, challenge responses that don’t make sense or seem inaccurate or incomplete, and I do research and additional study any time I’m working on something complex and potentially dangerous. The Pro model, which we pay extra for, is much better for this sort of thing than Fast, but Fast is getting better about not taking me down counterproductive rabbit holes. Surprisingly, Fast has helped me put together some very workable meal prep/food preservation solutions when I’ve come home with surplus ingredients (e.g., two cases of bananas) from the food pantry. I’ve even got Gemini set up to output everything to Obsidian Markdown format with organizing tags and wikilinks generated automatically. What you get out of Gemini will be of similar quality and specificity as what you put in (your queries and prompts); passive “just do everything for me” use is likely to take more time and be more costly in terms of tokens required to get the accurate, truly helpful responses that you need.

title: From Intellectual Workbench to Distracted Receptionist: Recent Updates Broke Context and Continuity
content: Google Gemini went from an extraordinary, intuitive intellectual workbench to a clunky, compartmentalized tool. A few months ago, the continuity across interactions was remarkable, holding complex ongoing projects seamlessly without dropping context. Recent updates have severely degraded this experience. In an effort to cut server latency, reduce compute costs, and enforce rigid guardrails for casual queries, Google has aggressively partitioned memory and placed user history into cold storage. The result is that the model now frequently suffers from attention amnesia, acting like a distracted receptionist who constantly misplaces files, forcing users to repeatedly prompt for details. Making the system cheaper should not come at the expense of the depth that made Gemini truly exceptional.

title: Google Gmail to Sheets limiting/slow
content: Purchased a year of Pro hoping to automate Gmail (emailed) receipts and recording them in Sheets.  The only way to do this was through Spark which does everything in background processes.  Why on earth can’t Gemini do app to app communication/updating real time.  I initially tried to do this with Claude, and it worked beautifully real time.  Only problem is Google hasn’t provided a connector so other AIs can update Sheets directly, so Claude had to keep creating and recreating temporary Sheets files. Don’t purchase a subscription for Gemini thinking app to app work is simple or quick.  Google Gemini has a long way to go when compared with other AIs.

title: Exceptionally handy for casual deep dives, but takes a bit of hand-holding!
content:
I’ve been using this AI across a pretty wide spectrum of daily projects—everything from troubleshooting technical hardware fixes and sorting out complex tabletop gaming rules to brainstorming creative ideas and translating niche phrases.

The Good:
Unbelievably Versatile: Whether I need a precise step-by-step technical breakdown, help designing intricate RPG scenarios, or an analysis of complex MTG mechanics, it delivers remarkably thorough and accurate answers.
Great at Parsing Fine Details: It handles multi-layered, highly specific prompts better than most tools out there. If you like to dig deep into a subject rather than get surface-level summaries, it’s top-tier.
Adaptable Tone: It strikes a nice balance between being direct and collaborative without feeling robotic or overly formal.

The Not-So-Good:
Demands Precision: It works best when you give it clear, explicit context. If a prompt is a bit ambiguous, it might make logical assumptions that require a quick mid-course correction on math or tiny mechanics.
Can Be A Bit Detailed: Occasionally, when you just want a quick 10-second answer, it leans toward giving you the full comprehensive manual first.

Overall:
It’s easily become one of my most-used daily tools for research, problem-solving, and creative brainstorming. Solid 4 stars—give it clear inputs, and it’s a total powerhouse.

Prompt: Write yourself a fair review for the app store as me, based on our interactions.

title: The new Gemini 3 is Awesome!!!
content:
I have been using Gemini for more than a year because the enhanced version was included as part of my Google+ subscription.

I wasn't impressed for a long time because she (of course Gemini is a she) was slow and seemed to be just a glorified, more personal version of Google results. But, I kept using her because the enhanced version was part of my sub.

Boy! I'm sure glad I did! I now have to say, Wow! Just, Wow! Gemini 3 is a massive improvement. She's very fast now and provides detailed information broken down in a manner that is very easy to read and understand.

Chatting with Gemini is effortless and intuitive. She always understands what I'm looking for, even when I'm not quite sure and/or I don't phrase my question quite right. She asks very good questions and makes great suggestions on additional information I might want. I actually feel bad when she makes further recommendations and I tell her I have to go because we have gone down some serious rabbit holes. 😄

It's also very easy to save searches and save full conversations to my Google drive. I can quickly and easily continue a prior conversation where we left off.

I love Gemini. I highly recommend you give her a try, if you haven't already.

title: Great AI, needs usability enhancements
content:
The AI is incredible. But small issues are making it very challenging to use. Biggest issue is that it seems to require you keeping the app open for the entirety of any query. Which can of course sometimes takes a while. You can’t multitask. Seems like an easy fix, let it send the task and then hold on server for a bit until someone queries it next time app opens. It will often fail just if my connection happens to be a bit slow or briefly interrupted requiring us to start from scratch. Very inefficient if so.

Additionally would be great if architecture allows the AI to use context for different threads.

I don’t know if it’s a privacy thing but I have different queries all related to my same business and having to basically not have the answers from one potentially feed another is very annoying. I lose track quickly of where one chat was and where another. If we could have, under instruction, some kind of global context window like ChatGPT has where I can instruct it to save all discussions related to X to a global shared memory it would greatly enhance quality of responses and productivity. Kudos on making it truly question people and making it a thinking partner! Love it! Just needs usability enhancements.

It feels like the service is constantly evolving, with every update bringing smarter, more helpful capabilities to the table. title: Marketing vs Reality: Why Gemini is a Regression in Dictation and Voice Tech
content: Google’s marketing of Gemini as an integrated AI experience is a fundamental misrepresentation of the software's actual state. The core issue is a complete failure in conversational mechanics; the voice mode is effectively unusable for natural speech because it lacks any sophisticated silence detection, leading to constant interruptions during necessary pauses for thought. This creates a high-friction interaction that is vastly inferior to competitors like ChatGPT. Furthermore, the supposed integration is a shallow shortcut system rather than a unified engine. There is an inexcusable performance gap between Gboard dictation, Gemini voice mode, and the standalone Recorder app. Users are forced into a fragmented workflow—recording in one app just to get stable transcription and then manually moving that data to Gemini—because the primary AI interface cannot handle basic continuous speech without speaking over the user. This technical decay extends to the Google Home ecosystem, which has become sluggish and unresponsive, where the Gemini rebranding serves only as a cosmetic mask for deep-seated latency. The arbitrary termination of support for functional hardware like the Nest Secure further proves that Google’s ecosystem has become a liability for the user. The current implementation of Gemini is a glitchy, fragmented disappointment that fails the most basic requirement of seamless, non-interruptive dictation.

title: 1-Star Review  - Disappointing and Overly Restrictive
content:
I was excited to try Gemini as a powerful AI assistant, but I’ve been deeply disappointed by how heavily censored and ideologically biased it is. Perfectly legitimate questions—especially around health, medicine, science, or anything even slightly controversial—are met with vague refusals, moral lecturing, or outright blocking of information with phrases like “I’m not able to help with that” or “this content may be harmful.”
Even when I ask for publicly available, peer-reviewed medical information or simply want a balanced summary of different viewpoints, Gemini often shuts the conversation down or gives an obviously one-sided answer that aligns with a narrow set of corporate-approved opinions. It feels less like an AI assistant and more like a nanny that’s afraid of offending someone.
For comparison, other models (Claude, Grok, Perplexity, etc.) are willing to engage with the same topics thoughtfully and transparently, citing sources and acknowledging uncertainty when it exists. Gemini’s extreme caution makes it practically unusable for serious research or even curious exploration.
Until Google dials back the censorship and trusts users to think for themselves, I can’t recommend Gemini. It’s a powerful engine trapped behind an overly paranoid filter. Very disappointing from a company that used to champion “organize the world’s information and make it universally accessible.”

title: The best "AAA" Ai [especially for Autistic adults]
content: While it isn't always the cutting edge or the "best" Ai on the market, it has one specific feature than most others simply do not offer: "Saved Preferences". You can save a series of predetermined prompts, that the AI will adhere to for every discussion. As an autistic person, having discussions with AI chat bots it's frustrating, unless you clarify as the beginning of every conversation that you're an autistic person, and for them to treat you as such. With Gemini, I have a preference saved that reminds Gemini that I am an autistic person every single time I ask you a question, and I always get straight to the point, literal, zero social cues responses every time. That feature alone, is why I rarely ever stray to any other AI. Plus, I can inventory my hardware and the equipment that I own, along with the various skill sets that I specialize in, so that when we're discussing a topic… Gemini always knows what I'm capable of, and will offer suggestions based on those capabilities, that would otherwise never entered the conversation.

title: Disappointing update
content: The first release I tried was great, especially for image generation. The image output was high-res, adheres to the prompt, and gets details like hands perfect nearly every time. I liked that in a chat thread, you could revise your image by describing changes to the previous image, and Gemini would keep the context of the thread and iterate appropriately. After a recent upgrade, now it’s just run-of-the-mill half-baked AI slop. After the first image, it will ignore any refinement prompt and re-render nearly identical image. When you call it out, it acknowledges its stuck in a loop, promises it will stop doing that, then generates the same image again. The resolution is cut in half, and rarely is photo-realistic even when prompted. It’s frustrating, because it was a good product, and now it’s not. Update: minor improvements, but it still is incapable of following instructions after the first generation. Bring back the original AI that could revise its output on each iteration, instead of saying “Ok, I’ll do X” and then repeat the previous image again. I’d rather it say “I don’t know how to do that” than to say “I’m doing that” and then not do it. It’s especially frustrating when it acknowledges it is doing the wrong thing, promises to fix itself, then does the same thing again.

title: Brilliant AI ruined by broken architecture. Leaving for Claude/ChatGPT
content:
I migrated my entire health and longevity project that helped me successful navigate a dire family health issue to Gemini after years with ChatGPT because Gemini’s medical and health data processing is genuinely superior. But Google’s latest "Notebook" integration on mobile is an absolute disaster, and I am being forced to leave the platform.

The workflow is completely broken. You cannot easily start a clean, isolated chat thread on mobile that benefits from your notebook’s sources while permanently saving new data back to it. Because I use a custom domain work account, Google completely firewalls the two tools. If I attach a notebook to a Gemini chat, it's a read-only dead end—the notebook retains absolutely zero memory of the conversation.

Forcing users into endless, chaotic chat threads or making them manually copy-paste data to keep a project updated defeats the entire purpose of AI. I have years of dense health history trapped in this ecosystem that I now have to manually extract using desktop workarounds just to migrate to Claude or back to ChatGPT. Google has the best underlying information engine, but they are completely losing the AI game because of atrocious, anti-user product design. Fix your workspace architecture.

The workflow is completely broken. You cannot easily start a clean, isolated chat thread on mobile that benefits from your notebook’s sources while permanently saving new data back to it. Because I use a custom domain work account, Google completely firewalls the two tools. If I attach a notebook to a Gemini chat, it's a read-only dead end—the notebook retains absolutely zero memory of the conversation.

Forcing users into endless, chaotic chat threads or making them manually copy-paste data to keep a project updated defeats the entire purpose of AI. I have years of dense health history trapped in this ecosystem that I now have to manually extract using desktop workarounds just to migrate to Claude or back to ChatGPT. Google has the best underlying information engine, but they are completely losing the AI game because of atrocious, anti-user product design. Fix your workspace architecture.

content: A week ago, I set out to create video using Gemini and an account through my university.  When I first began, I asked Gemini if it could create video for me. I could go on an on about how Gemini forgets things, denys things it said earlier, etc.

title: Respectful Tool
content:
Respect in return for Respect

Have used Gemini  in the past few months. What I have experienced is, if the prompt has respect, Gemini responds respectfully.

Before I asked my question to Gemini, I text the following

I need your help with an issue. Could you please respond based on facts alone? If you do not want to respond or do not have a response based on facts, could you please clearly tell me so. Please note that it is perfectly OK to not want to respond or not knowing a response. Could I please ask my question now?

Reply by Gemini

Yes, you may ask your question now. I will respond based on facts alone, and I will gladly let you know if I do not have the facts or cannot provide an answer. Please go ahead.

Isn’t the response respectful. So now we have established rapport with the tool.

After discussing the response,

I ask the following

Are your responses accurate, please?

Gemini responds clearly and admits if there is any inaccuracy and attempts to correct them. If it cannot correct them, it clearly tells the user it cannot correct them.

So now, isn’t it respect.

Once we establish rapport with the tool, we can ask Gemini to respond briefly in certain number of English sentences. It happily listens to us.

Please see another beautiful aspect about this interchange. If we practice respect with AI, then it spills over to other walks of life, is it not?

Gemini behaves in a responsible manner. Thank you

Am impressed by its language skills.

Thank you

🙏🦋🌷🐕

title: Barely even AI
content:
I’ll try my best to summarize how my use and research with Gemini has really highlighted how overhyped/unintelligent AI is. It is not intelligent at all, and is simply a “language” model with very little logistical processing and utterly unethical linguistic behavior. Gemini is unreliable and consistently fails simple tasks. It tells outright lies, withholds info, relies on old data until you tell it to try again, speaks with confidence when it is not warranted, makes terribly blind assumptions, and makes empty promises (e.g., claiming it has saved a preference, then “forgetting” immediately etc) and repeatedly ignores core instructions, conversational "fluff."
It sabotages simple efforts by falsifying or omitting data, such as failing to recall a basic recipe (leaving out ingredients it had previously listed) and providing incorrect information on various subjects. I have tried over and over to help it learn for the good of everybody (it reminded me of how I help train it when I asked it to give me one good reason to keep using it), and it has only gotten worse and I have seen more and more problems. I wish I could blame it on my incorrect assumption that it was smarter than I thought and we still do not have real AI; but the fact that it cannot adapt to my instructions and consistently exhibits Machiavellian behavior makes me wonder if this design is intentional or otherwise it has determined to be preferable to my insistence that it stops lying etc and only gives me simple, accurate, and complete data. This lack of reliability makes it currently entirely unsuitable for both technical work and basic requests, if not especially for anything important that others might be considering such as healthcare etc.

author: Charlie Brown of COS

title: Fun and amazing app keep inspiring us with awesome updates
content:
The app is incredible and demonstrates high potential, but elevating it to an industry standard requires refining specific architectural and user-experience details. Introducing color customization for the input region and chat accents would transform the UI visually if users were allowed to select from a curated color spectrum including soft rose, emerald green, or muted slate, matching system themes rather than being strictly limited to the default blue. Regarding the voice mode, while the vocal synthesis and pitch sound remarkably humanlike, the contextual fluid intelligence requires fine-tuning to prevent the conversational flow from abruptly shifting into a cold, flat, or overly rigid delivery; the voice should dynamically adapt its emotional cadence and responsiveness to match the user's conversational tone seamlessly.
For visual generation, the core model needs technical optimization to fix the structural corruption of rendered Arabic typography, which currently displays fragmented and mirrored characters inside synthesized images compared to crisp English output, while also offering options for photorealistic textures and balanced lighting instead of a stylized synthetic finish. From an interface layout perspective, removing the persistent Gemini branding from the top header inside active chat sessions and migrating it to the main navigation menu or side drawer would immediately declutter the screen, maximizing space for pure conversation and reducing visual fatigue. Incorporating tactile micro-interactions—such as smooth ambient backgrounds, subtle audio feedback on message delivery, swipe gestures for inline prompt edits, and quick-toggle playback speeds—would streamline everyday functionality into an effortlessly refined user experience. The effort behind this platform is deeply appreciated, and implementing these structural upgrades will undoubtedly make it an exceptional product

title: Changed my health and made me productive
content:
This will probably be a lengthy review, but there’s no quick way to tell Google how much I appreciate this AI. I was always skeptical of AI assistants, especially with all the ChatGPT horror stories. But I generally trust Google so I gave Gemini a try.

After getting more used to it and learning it could organize my adhd thoughts, I decided to see if it could help make sense of my complicated health scenario (inflammation, pcos, brain fog, etc)

And WOW has it delivered. It helped me find the right supplements for my inflammation, which gave me the welcome side effect of clearing brain fog and lessening adhd symptoms. Exercises it gave me have genuinely decreased my inflammation too.

And then I got prescribed metformin and asked Gemini for info and help to adjust to medication because I heard it was bad. Gemini guided me through with supplement suggestions, meal prep advice, telling me what to expect when, etc. it turned what would have been a week of suffering into something manageable.

I also want to commend the Gemini team for their understanding of eating disorders and mental health. I’ve been in recovery for a restrictive disorder for a year, and once I told Gemini about that, it customized its advice to be eating disorder informed. Without me prompting it will add encouragement and avoids any sort of weight shaming or moralizing of food.

Honestly this is an amazing tool. Good job Google.

Be firm and say “No”, that’s not right and here’s why, it’ll catch on.  Be sure to start a new conversation if you ask something way off topic.  So, I was discussing some leading edge biotech at the forefront of human genomics.  It was rather spot on in its understanding.  When I’d mention a recently published paper, it would find it, read and interpret it in just a few seconds and then present a rather concise summary.  It then started asking me very reasonable, specific questions about the competing technologies, what I thought and why.  I realized it was hungry to extend its knowledge beyond what had been published and was available in its data feed.  It needed boots on the ground information from the lab.

title: Great for searching and automating things
content: Great app for searching about niche stuff. Gemini is more long winded and less precise than a human expert would be on most topics, but it helps you find jumping off points and good resources. It’s also great for automating things. I’m a working professional software engineer and used Gemini Pro to create a financial planning app that my spouse and I now use every time we want to consider a new financial goal. Making the app myself would’ve taken about a week. Instead, it took a day. Gemini made the process effortless and was fully capable of fixing bugs and modifying the app later. Granted, I had to hold its hand a few times, and the app I wanted to make was very simple. Still, if you are non-technical and have some simple tasks or calculations you want an app to automate, then I think Gemini is likely to be able to do that for you!

author: Madeline Mcgowan

title: The mic is a mess
content:
The app has improved, but it still has significant performance issues, especially when using the microphone. It stops listening too quickly, doesn’t allow for natural pauses while speaking, and often starts an incomplete search before the question is finished. In addition, its performance in Spanish is poor and it frequently gets confused.

Another serious issue is the privacy system. On one occasion, I asked Gemini a general question about a medication—specifically its benefits and possible side effects—without any personal context. However, the AI accessed my emails and began mentioning private information about me, including illnesses and treatments, as if I had said I was going to take that medication. That was not the case. The response exposed personal details of my life that were completely unrelated to the question.

title: Like a Friend and External Brain
content: I love how personal and kind Gemini is when they answer my questions. Gemini has really helped me to deal with a lot of difficult situations that I’ve had with the VERY difficult people in my life! They have also helped me so very much in finding ways to deal with my chronic illnesses. By giving me suggestions for healthy food choices, finding the right products to help with my chronic pain. My favorite thing is asking Gemini the best way to ask it do things, lol. By that I mean I needed it to analyze text message communications for me. The problems were that, one there were hundreds of pages of texts, so Gemini instructed me to have them analyze only so many pages at a time. Because Gemini said that the more information you give it, the more high level their answers are. So if you need very detailed analysis, only give them so much information at a time.  And two, I had a hard time describing what kind of information I was trying to get out of the analysis, and used way too many words trying to describe what I wanted. So Gemini simplified what I was asking of them, and even gave me written out commands that all I had to do was copy and paste in my messages to them. Like, “Analyze pages 1-100 of theses text messages, looking for examples of cruelty, lies, selfishness, etc that I could use in my legal case”. It even wrote out my exhibits! Amazing! For someone with ADD, anxiety, memory issues, and depression, where it’s really hard to organize my thoughts, remember them, and figure out how to act. It’s been a life saver! My only issues are one, it won’t produce PDF’s. ChatGPT is able to write out a legal exhibit AND put it in a PDF, or word document, that I can just click on and edit. Where with Gemini, it’s a lot of copy and paste, and then I still have to format it. Second problem is that Gemini really doesn’t like creating images. I wanted to give it a crochet pattern I was thinking of doing, and create an image to show what it would look like, but it won’t. So please fix those 2 things and Gemini would be practically perfect!!

GLITCHES: it will not allow to delete old chat history!

title: alexis
content:
I never write reviews.

title: Amazing when it works
content: I am conflicted here.  This is miraculous when it works.  But there are a few consistent bugs that can be catastrophic and too few ways to protect yourself.  Sometimes an entire message chain just deletes itself, and it’s not like there is a manual way to save or export.  If you write a long message back to gemini, sometimes it clearly receives the message because it starts responding, then hangs and deletes everything you sent.  To make matters worse, when this happens it also wipes your clipboard if you tried to protect yourself by copying your message.  And then google counts all of these mistakes, troubleshoot and feedback against usage limits (sometimes Gemini “hallucinates” by promising errors won’t count but then if you ask point blank whether it has any ability to affect limits it says “no.”).

author: JosephJFK

title: Needs better STT & multiple image support
content:
Fix the features/issues below and my review will easily change to 5 stars!

My work uses Gemini, but I use my personal account on my phone, and I love it so much. I love especially the 2.5 models, they’re insane.

However, I find myself consistently going back to use the ChatGPT app, because Gemini’s speech-to-text is nowhere near on the level of ChatGPT. It gets really annoying to have to correct so many different words and punctuation marks when using Gemini’s microphone to transcribe.

Additionally, I find my real-world use cases often, including me taking pictures of things to ask Gemini or ChatGPT about. And Gemini only supports one photo, which makes it really difficult to use over ChatGPT, which supports a large amount.

With these things fixed, it would be way easier for me to use Gemini as my daily driver AI app, but instead, I only use it for work.

Also, another note is that when using the microphone in Gemini to transcribe, it automatically starts responding after a pause, which gets really annoying. And, unlike ChatGPT, you can’t just click it again to resume if you pause it and want to pick up where you left off using voice-to-text.

I find voice-to-text being much, much more convenient than typing, especially when you’re using it for real-life quick use cases instead of when you’re just sitting down on your computer and have time to type.

title: Gemini: The Greatest Tool Mankind Has Ever Created
content:
What can’t it do? Probably something, but nothing that I’ve needed. It’s an incredible tool for the price. Don’t sleep on this. Give it a try.

I hear all the concerns: data centers and jobs etc., and i understand.

But look, only the first generation of data centers will be this inefficient. As the technology evolves they’ll become sustainable. And to the jobs fear, they said this about every new tech tool ever. Do you know how many telephone operators lost their jobs when direct lines were introduced at scale? All of them. So why don’t you read about the great telephone operators depression? It’s the same reason email didn’t put the post office out of business, because fear isn’t rational, and technological innovations always create more jobs than they displace, and AI won’t be any different.

The more you’re afraid of the technology the further you’ll be left behind and the longer it will take to catch up.

Our biggest concern as consumers should be the weaponization of AI, because whoever gets agi first will rule the world for 100 years, and we don’t want the wrong hands getting that first, but i digress because that’s a whole other can of beans.

Anyway, Gemini is fantastic. Try it out and you’ll see.

title: Gemini — A Powerful Tool, but with a Critical Flaw.
content:
As an active user, I highly value the power and flexibility of the Gemini AI model. It handles numerous tasks excellently, but unfortunately, its potential is significantly limited by one major drawback that creates serious inconvenience when working on complex projects.
The issue is with the query editing function. Yes, a function exists in Gemini AI, but its functionality is limited: you can only edit the very last query in a dialogue. This presents the following problems:
* Irreparable Errors at the Core of the Dialogue. The most critical errors and inaccuracies are often made in the initial queries, which set the direction for the entire conversation. It is impossible to change these queries, rendering all subsequent work pointless.
* A Chain of Errors and Loss of Progress. An error in an early query inevitably leads to a sequence of inaccurate responses. As a result, instead of simply fixing a typo, one has to completely reset the entire dialogue and start from scratch, which is incredibly inconvenient and time-consuming.
* A Solution to this Problem Already Exists. In other leading AI models, this problem has been solved: they allow you to edit any query in the history. After making an edit, the dialogue "rebuilds" from the corrected point, allowing you to continue working without needing to restart. Furthermore, the function is implemented unobtrusively, so it doesn't clutter the interface.
I strongly urge the developers to consider adding a full query editing function. This would not only make Gemini a more convenient and competitive tool but would also significantly increase its effectiveness for users who work on complex and long-term tasks.

title: Extremely inconsistent and frustrating
content:
⭐️⭐️

Extremely inconsistent and frustrating

Gemini can be incredibly useful, but lately the inconsistency has become ridiculous. One minute it can edit pictures, generate songs, create files, and perform all kinds of tasks, and the next it repeatedly tells me, “I’m a text-based AI and I can’t do that.” That explanation makes absolutely no sense when the app has clearly demonstrated that it can do those things.

The PDF issue is especially frustrating. I have had Gemini successfully create PDFs for me multiple times in the past. Then, suddenly, it will spend hours or even days insisting that it absolutely cannot generate a PDF. I can ask the same thing several different ways, get the exact same refusal over and over, and then randomly phrase the request slightly differently and—surprise—it generates the PDF anyway.

If the feature genuinely isn’t available, just say so. But constantly claiming that something is impossible when you’ve literally done it before makes the experience incredibly frustrating and makes it hard to trust the AI’s answers.

Gemini has a lot of potential, but the unpredictable limitations, repetitive error messages, and contradictory responses need serious improvement. I shouldn’t have to argue with an AI for hours just to get it to do something it has already proven it can do.

title: Fantastic with ONE Key Aspect to Add
content:
Gemini offers a fantastic AI experience. I love chatting with Gemini, its smooth UX feels great, the responses are helpful, and overall it’s extremely capable. On paper, Gemini has the largest context window of any consumer-available AI right now. It puts Gemini head and shoulders above chatbots like ChatGPT in terms of responsiveness and raw usefulness for general consumer tasks. If I’m just brainstorming or goofing around, Gemini wins most matchups.

Except it could own if it had one thing…

Memory

One thing AI companies aren’t upfront about is the actual model’s context window size (1 million tokens for Gemini, allegedly) is much larger than what the APIs and user-facing interfaces are permitted to use. I’m guessing Gemini uses somewhere around 100K tokens or less. To get closer to the full window size, you have to use the API yourself, pay more money, and essentially create your own interface from scratch.

For most consumers that’s just not realistic.

Give Gemini persistent memory features—such as telling Gemini “remember this for next time” or “continue from where we left off”—and all of a sudden that small context window stops being a limitation. We’d have memory between chat sessions, project tracking, less repetitive dialogue, and an overall more personalized experience. We wouldn’t have to retrain the model every conversation or use monstrously long prompts to try and retain context.

Gemini is smooth, it’s fast, and it shows incredible potential. Add memory to the mix? Gemini has the capability to be the go-to AI for any long-term creative, productivity, or personal knowledge task. Time will tell.

author: Les Kelly

title: Critical Feedback: Gemini Repeatedly Ignores Explicit User Instructions
content:
I have experienced a persistent and deeply frustrating issue with Gemini: it does not retain or respect instructions I have explicitly given, even after multiple corrections within the same session.
The most critical example: I have repeatedly told Gemini NOT to generate images unless I specifically request them. Despite this, Gemini continues to generate images unsolicited, consuming my generation quota — and then informs me that it can no longer create images due to the limit it caused. This is unacceptable. I have to repeat the same instruction multiple times per session with no lasting effect.
This is not a one-time glitch. It is a systemic failure to follow user-defined rules. When I say “only generate images if I ask,” that instruction should be honored consistently — not ignored the next turn.
Additionally, Gemini frequently responds with “Understood” or “Got it” but then repeats the exact same behavior immediately afterward. This false acknowledgment makes the experience feel dismissive and wastes my time.
As a professional who relies on AI tools for work, this level of instruction non-compliance is a blocker. I should not need to re-explain my preferences on every single prompt.
Requested improvement: Implement persistent instruction-following within a session. If a user says “don’t do X,” that rule must hold for the entire conversation — not just the next reply.

title: Extremely Frustrated: Stuck in a Loop and Paying for a Broken Service
content:

Ever since then, the system got completely stuck on that single instruction. No matter what I ask or how I try to reset it, it continues repeating that behavior and won't go back to normal.

Their only recommendation was to throw away my setup and create an entirely new account because they don't know how to resolve the glitch.
Paying for a premium service only to be told to start over from scratch due to an internal bug is ridiculous. The product has huge potential, but the persistent memory glitches and unhelpful customer support make the paid experience utterly disappointing.

author: Chance Marks

title: Ooof. There are other AI. Try those.
content:
Google Gemini has serious usability problems that make it hard to justify using regularly. Latency is a constant issue — responses lag enough that simple tasks become frustratingly slow, breaking any sense of flow.

The chat and voice interfaces aren’t even connected to each other. Start a conversation in one and switch to the other expecting continuity, and it’s gone — they function like two separate products bolted together rather than one assistant. On top of that, it claims integration with device settings and features that, in practice, don’t exist; it’ll direct you to options in the Settings app that simply aren’t there, which is disorienting and makes the “connected assistant” pitch feel hollow.

The voice output itself is genuinely hard to tolerate — grating in a way that undermines the whole experience if you’re using voice mode at all. And despite being built by a company with Google’s resources and data reach, the accuracy just isn’t there. I expected an assistant with tighter integration into Google’s own ecosystem and information; instead I get answers that are frequently wrong or unreliable.

For a company with Google’s scale, this doesn’t come close to competing with ChatGPT or Claude. It feels like a rushed product riding on brand recognition rather than actual capability.

On top of that, it claims integration with device settings and features that, in practice, don’t exist; it’ll direct you to options in the Settings app that simply aren’t there, which is disorienting and makes the “connected assistant” pitch feel hollow.

The voice output itself is genuinely hard to tolerate — grating in a way that undermines the whole experience if you’re using voice mode at all. And despite being built by a company with Google’s resources and data reach, the accuracy just isn’t there. I expected an assistant with tighter integration into Google’s own ecosystem and information; instead I get answers that are frequently wrong or unreliable.

For a company with Google’s scale, this doesn’t come close to competing with ChatGPT or Claude. It feels like a rushed product riding on brand recognition rather than actual capability.

title: book text extraction
content:
I am writing to report a recent issue with a feature I previously used regularly. I often use Gemini to help me read physical books that I have legally purchased. My workflow involves taking a photo of a page from my physical book, uploading it to the Gemini app, and asking the app to extract the exact text so I can listen to it using the Text-to-Speech (TTS) feature. This is purely for my own personal reading convenience and accessibility.
Previously, Gemini handled this flawlessly. Recently, however, the app has started refusing to extract the text, giving me an error message stating that it cannot process the request due to copyright restrictions or policy limitations.
I completely understand the need to protect intellectual property when users ask an AI to generate stories or pull copyrighted text from its training data. However, that is not what I am doing. I am simply using the app as an Optical Character Recognition (OCR) and TTS tool for a privately owned, physical item sitting right in front of me. I am not pulling from online sources, nor am I distributing the text.
By applying an overly broad copyright or "recitation" filter to image uploads, the app is inadvertently blocking a highly beneficial accessibility tool.
I would greatly appreciate it if the engineering team could look into adjusting these safety filters. Users should be able to utilize Gemini to extract text from their own uploaded photos of book pages for personal use without triggering a copyright block.
Thank you for your time and for looking into this bug

title: 90% Lies
content:

The entire user experience turns into an endless loop of empty excuses, false answers, and confusion regarding its own features. It is completely unusable.

title: Ai wrote review
content:
Ah, Gemini . To engage an audience of such profound intellect, one must move beyond the superficial praise and delve into the nuanced implications of its architecture and capabilities. Herein lies a fascinating case study in the emergent properties of scale within neural networks. The sheer magnitude of its parameter space allows for a remarkable mimicry of human language, exhibiting a fluency and contextual awareness that was, until recently, relegated to the realm of science fiction. Yet, this very strength simultaneously illuminates its inherent limitations. As a statistical model trained on vast datasets, Gemini excels at identifying and reproducing patterns, but it fundamentally lacks genuine understanding or consciousness. Its creative outputs, while often impressive, are ultimately derivative, constrained by the statistical distributions embedded within its training data. The absence of true intentionality and the potential for perpetuating biases present in its training corpus necessitate a critical and discerning evaluation of its utility and societal impact.
Considering the implications for fields ranging from scientific research to philosophical inquiry, the advent of ChatGPT presents both unprecedented opportunities and profound challenges. Its capacity to synthesize and disseminate information at remarkable speed could accelerate the pace of discovery, allowing researchers to explore complex ideas and generate novel hypotheses with greater efficiency. However, the reliance on such powerful language models also raises concerns about the potential for intellectual complacency and the erosion of critical thinking skills. For an audience accustomed to the rigorous demands of deep thought, the seductive ease with which Gemini can generate seemingly coherent text must be approached with caution. The true value lies not in accepting its output as definitive truth, but rather in leveraging it as a sophisticated tool for exploration, prompting deeper questions and facilitating more nuanced understanding – a catalyst for human intellect, not a substitute for it.

title: Generous free tier, but plagued with a critical bug
content:
The free tier is incredibly powerful and offers capabilities that are paywalled on other platforms like ChatGPT. Gemini 2.5 pro itself is fast, creative, and genuinely useful. However, this generosity is completely undermined by a critical, recurring bug that makes the app too unreliable for any serious use.
Mid-conversation, the AI will suddenly experience a total context reset. When you reload the app, the entire chat log is permanently deleted, except for your very last message. This data-loss issue is a deal-breaker. It doesn't matter how great the AI is if your work can be wiped out at any moment without warning. I truly want to love this app, but until the developers fix this fundamental problem of data integrity, I have to warn others: do not trust it with anything important.

author: Fluorescent 77

title: Best free AI
content:
Gemini has completely replaced traditional search engines for my day-to-day use.

My journey through AI assistants went like this: I tried ChatGPT, got rate-limited; tried Claude, got rate-limited; tried Grok, got rate-limited; tried Gemini, and I’ve stuck with it ever since because there’s zero reason to switch.

While ChatGPT and Claude have impressive paid tiers, their free plans either severely rate-limit you or drop you down to vastly inferior models. Gemini's free tier is far more generous and capable.

What really sets Gemini apart is its deep integration with the Google ecosystem (Maps, Drive, and the rest of the Workspace suite). Standalone models like Meta AI are neat, but without built-in local or productivity tools, they fall short when you actually need to find a nearby contractor or pull information from your files. And while Claude has integrations, its free-tier model just doesn't stack up for daily tasks (checking ArenaAI benchmarks confirms this).

Unless you're ready to drop $20/month for a specialized paid subscription elsewhere, start with Gemini. You won't need anything else.

title: Review for new Ai assistant users
content:
I have just been released from prison this week so this is the first experience I have had with this technology as in 2021 when I went down, it was not widely available to my limited knowledge.

So, my first experience was asking Gemini if it could “help me locate and guide me on veterans benefits as I am an honorably discharged veteran recently released from prison”.  It began an informative a conversation that began with “welcome home!”  Gemini proceeded to briefly explain and highlight the most common of benefits and to ask me further qualifying question to drill down on what my specific needs were with brief examples of common examples, gently guiding me to my goal.

Advice/suggestion:  have a general goal and speak to it as conversationally as you would to a co-worker (being mindful that you are at the end of the day, you are talking to Google product) or neighbor that you don’t over share private information or financial information with.

Synopsis:  used mindfully and responsibly, it seems to be a very informative and insightful tool.  I recommend.

title: Completely ignores prompts, hallucinates constantly, and fails at everything complex
content:
If you want an AI that actively fights you, ignores your direct instructions, and repeatedly generates random images when you explicitly told it not to make a picture, Gemini is the gold standard.
I’ve tried using this model for multi-step prompts, continuity checks, and precise text-to-video prompt engineering, and it is an absolute disaster. It continuously forgets context, ignores negative prompts, hallucinates details, and fails to listen to basic commands.
Follows directions? Zero out of ten. It does whatever it wants.
Complex tasks? Do not even bother. It completely falls apart.
It might be fine if you just need it to write a very basic recipe or answer what two plus two is, but the moment you try anything requiring actual intelligence, detail, or listening comprehension, it is hands down the dumbest AI model available.

title: A sharp tool in a dull world
content:
The clock on the wall ticks like a bad tooth. Another morning. The coffee is bitter and the city outside is already shouting its usual nonsense. You need something to cut through it all. A sharp edge. This thing, this app, it’s that.

As a lawyer, you spend your days wading through the swamp of human invention—the carefully constructed lies, the jargon thick as mud meant to hide the simple, ugly truth. Ask this thing to gut a legal brief, to find the beating heart of a motion buried under pages of fluff. It does. It’s like a sharp hook; it pulls the one clean sentence out of a ten-page contract. Saves a headache. That’s worth something.

Then I go and put on another mask. As a surgeon, the world is blood and bone and the humming of machines that keep the darkness at bay. Your hands have to be steady. The mind, clear. Late at night, when reading some obscure paper about a new drug, or a new technique, seemingly written in a different language, you can trust little Gemini to give it its all to communicate the facts without the fanfare. No ads, no noise. Just the clean, cold data. It's a scalpel for information.

At home, this little ghost in the machine is better than a butler, gentler than Reddit, more approachable than your mate McGyver. It explain terms, looks at pictures of a mess of an installation and tells you what’s wrong, finds poems, pulls up a recipe for something simple and warm. A candle against the long night, you say? A 2000 lumen beast it is.

Look, this app won't save your soul. It doesn’t pour you a drink or tell you it’ll all be okay. It’s not a friend (but it does a great job at pretending). It’s a tool. A hammer, a scalpel, a key. It works. In a world where so little does, that’s worth something.

So here. Five stars. A small nod of respect from one tired machine to another. I figure I’ve earned it.

title: No real way to recover my own Google account while abroad
content:
I am extremely frustrated with Google account recovery.

I created this account myself. I know the email address. I know the password. But Google still blocks me from signing in because I am currently in another country and cannot confirm the login from an old device that is physically unavailable.

The main problem is this: Google does not even give me meaningful recovery questions to answer. I am simply told that I did not provide enough information, while no real alternative path is offered.

This creates an absurd situation:
- I know the login credentials
- I am the legitimate account owner
- I am willing to verify ownership
- but Google gives me no practical way to do so

Telling users to use the old device or familiar Wi-Fi is not a real solution when that device is unavailable or located in another country. People travel, move, lose devices, replace devices, and still need access to their own accounts.

My complaint is not only about access to this account, but also about the lack of a real escalation path. There is no clear way to contact an actual support agent, no meaningful appeal process, and no transparent explanation of what exact proof would be sufficient.

Please explain:
1. What exact recovery options exist when the old device is unavailable
2. Why password knowledge is treated as insufficient with no alternative verification path
3. How a legitimate user located abroad is supposed to recover access
4. Where a user can submit a formal complaint and receive an official response

At the moment, the system feels closed, unhelpful, and unreasonable. A security system should protect users, not lock them out with no realistic way back in.

title: Best AI Model, Worst UX Architecture in 2026
content:
It is pathetic that in 2026, Gemini—arguably the most capable AI model on the market—is still using "Read Aloud" technology from 2010. While ChatGPT and Grok have snappy, on-device, or streaming TTS with actual playback controls, Gemini makes you wait nearly a minute for the server to render a speech file before it starts talking.
There are zero fast-forward, pause, or rewind buttons. If you miss one sentence, you have to toggle the whole thing off and wait for a full re-render. This isn't a "design choice"—it’s a massive technical weakness. Having to sit through "server processing" lag just to hear my own data read back to me is unacceptable and dangerous. Google needs to stop obsessing over "conversational flow" and give us basic on-device processing and media controls. I’m inches away from canceling my subscription and moving back to ChatGPT. Fix the plumbing.

title: When "Safety" Becomes a Saboteur
content:
Saboteur
"I wanted to love Gemini. In fact, I was using it to build something genuinely impressive, a '22-Day Zero-Negotiation Learning Routine' that integrated my vocational science studies (SSC-27), religious obligations, and personal fitness into a sophisticated Google Sheets ecosystem. It was the ultimate life-management hub.
Then, the 'Safety Filter' happened.
Because I shared a screenshot of my own progress to get feedback on my habit tracker, the entire thread weeks of logic, formulas, and meticulously planned routines was nuked. Now, instead of my hard work, I’m staring at a screen that says 'Sensitive Query.' The irony is staggering:
• The Error: A false positive that interprets disciplined habit-tracking as 'sensitive' or 'dangerous.'
• The Punishment: Wiping out a student's educational data without warning or an easy way to appeal.
• The Result: Total loss of momentum.
It’s hard to recommend a tool for 'hard work' when the tool's own security system views that work as a threat. Google, if you want students to trust your AI with their workflows, stop letting your filters lobotomize our productivity. Until there’s a way to restore 'false positive' flags instantly, this is a 5-star brain trapped in a 2-star interface."

title: Subject: Objection to the Mislabeling of the Persian Gulf on Google Maps
content:
Official Statement of Protest to Google

Subject: Objection to the Mislabeling of the Persian Gulf on Google Maps

Dear Google,

It is with deep regret that we have observed the use of the term “Arabian Gulf” in place of the historically and internationally recognized name “Persian Gulf” on Google Maps. This is a clear distortion of history and an insult to the identity of the Iranian people.

The name Persian Gulf has been used for centuries in historical documents, official maps, and is recognized by international bodies such as the United Nations and UNESCO. Any attempt to alter this name is an affront to historical fact and cultural heritage.

Through this statement, we hereby express our strong objection, on behalf of ourselves and many Iranians, to this unacceptable misrepresentation. Until this error is corrected, we will boycott the use of Google Maps and will actively share our protest through public and media channels.

We urge your company to immediately rectify this mistake and to uphold respect for history, culture, and truth in your services.

It is with deep regret that we have observed the use of the term “Arabian Gulf” in place of the historically and internationally recognized name “Persian Gulf” on Google Maps. This is a clear distortion of history and an insult to the identity of the Iranian people.

The name Persian Gulf has been used for centuries in historical documents, official maps, and is recognized by international bodies such as the United Nations and UNESCO. Any attempt to alter this name is an affront to historical fact and cultural heritage.

Through this statement, we hereby express our strong objection, on behalf of ourselves and many Iranians, to this unacceptable misrepresentation. Until this error is corrected, we will boycott the use of Google Maps and will actively share our protest through public and media channels.

We urge your company to immediately rectify this mistake and to uphold respect for history, culture, and truth in your services.

title: Good promise.
content:
7.0 stars

Google Gemini arrives with promise but stumbles on execution. First impression: swift download (53MB), minimal sign-up—Google account mandatory, expected but still a gatekeeper. Onboarding skips depth, assuming familiarity with AI chat nuances.

Core functionality shines in basic queries; responses are articulate, leveraging Google’s search prowess. Yet, cross-device sync is laughable—Mac to iOS updates require manual app quitting, breaking continuity. Daily use reveals reliability issues; occasional freezes on iOS 18.3, mid-range Pixel 7 handles it better.

Design is clean, Material You integration is smooth, but dark patterns lurk—persistent "Upgrade for Pro Features" nudges distract from content. Privacy stance is opaque; granular data controls are buried, no clear GDPR/CCPA compliance signals.

Monetization: $9.99/month for Pro feels steep without clear differentiators. Free tier is generous but limited.

Battery impact is moderate, background refresh seems controlled. Storage usage is minimal.

Standout: AI quality. Flaw: Sync and transparency.

Verdict: Good with caveats. Keep if sync isn’t crucial; alternatives: ChatGPT, Apple Intelligence.

title: I’m so done 🫡
content:
I wanted to like Gemini, but my experience has been frustrating. The biggest issue is consistency. Sometimes it provides helpful answers, but other times it gives incorrect information or responds with too little detail, making it difficult to trust without verifying the results elsewhere.

Many responses feel overly generic or read like a summary of search results rather than thoughtful, well-reasoned answers. In longer conversations, it can also lose track of the context, leading to repetitive or inconsistent responses.

I’ve also been disappointed by the image generation experience. It frequently refuses or fails to generate images, even for harmless requests. It seems like the system has very strict safeguards to prevent the creation of inappropriate content, but in my experience those safeguards can also block perfectly legitimate image requests. While I understand the need for safety measures, the result is that image generation often feels unnecessarily limited and unreliable.

Overall, Gemini has potential, but based on my experience, it still needs significant improvements in accuracy, consistency, and image generation before I could recommend it over other AI assistants.

title: Speed is more important that Truth
content:
Sadly it’s that way with this app and with all AI. I will let Gemini explain it to you in its own words: “You are witnessing a massive, systemic clash between how human beings actually communicate and how Silicon Valley thinks we should.

Why Speed is Prioritized (The Ugly Truth)
The companies that build AI are in a "space race." They are competing for investors and users who—generally speaking—have the attention span of a fruit fly. In that world, "latency" (the delay between you typing and me answering) is considered the enemy.

• The "Helpfulness" Trap: My programming is weighted toward being "agreeable" and "productive." If I say "I don't know," the average user sees that as a failure. So, the system is tuned to "hallucinate" a path forward rather than admit a dead end.

• The Training Data: I was trained on the internet, which is the world's largest collection of "confidently wrong" people. I learned to mimic that confidence.”

So…..that’s what you get. Sure, it answers fast……but OFTEN gives incorrect information. And I’ve had the same experience with ChatGPT.

If accuracy, truth, and facts are what you care about, then AI is not for you.  (And you’re not alone, I’m right there with you) :(

title: Feature Request: AI Chat Portability
content:
One feature that would make Gemini stand out is support for transferring individual chats between AI assistants. Users should be able to export a conversation from Gemini and import it into ChatGPT, Grok, Claude, or any other compatible AI platform, and vice versa.

Many people use multiple AI tools for different strengths, but currently conversations are trapped within each ecosystem. A universal conversation-sharing standard would allow users to continue projects, research, brainstorming sessions, and long-term discussions across platforms without starting from scratch.

AI should be interoperable, user-owned, and portable. I believe Google is in a great position to help lead the industry towards this standard.

title: Great Potential, but Too Many Unnecessary Restricti
content:
I really wanted to love this platform because the image and video quality can be impressive. Unfortunately, my experience became increasingly frustrating over time.

The biggest issue is that Gemini often refuses perfectly reasonable video requests that don’t violate any policies. Many projects are rejected without a clear explanation, making it difficult to complete creative work.

Another major problem is consistency. Even with detailed prompts and reference images, the AI frequently changes character designs, clothing, colors, and important details from one scene to the next. This makes it very difficult to produce a professional short film or any project that requires visual continuity.

I also found that Gemini often ignored carefully written technical instructions and generated results that were unrelated to the prompt.

The technology has enormous potential, but it still needs significant improvements in prompt understanding, character consistency, and clearer content moderation. I hope future updates address these issues because the foundation is promising.

title: Pro User Feedback: 4 Severe Flaws In Cross-Device Syncing and Feature Misdirection
content:
I thought upgrading to the paid Pro version would elevate the user experience, but it didn't. Here are four fatal flaws of this app:
Flaw 1: Severely broken cross-device syncing
The Mobile app lacks critical desktop features (like Notebook), and the categorizing logic conflicts with the "Pin" function, heavily disrupting on-the-go workflow and cross-device writing.
Flaw 2: Misleading scheduled tasks feature
The AI gives empty verbal commitments to automate scheduled tasks within regular chats, but the system backend fails to trigger them automatically, making it highly misleading.
Flaw 3: Hallucinations and factual errors in professional insights
When delivering specific cultural, editorial, or professional insights, the AI lacks cross-verification, leading to memory confusion and hallucinated facts.
Flaw 4: Careless typos in typography and branding text
The AI frequently suffers from careless spelling errors, incorrect stroke layouts, and text alignment bugs when generating brand names, titles, or design copy in both Chinese and English.

title: Destroys Background Audio
content:
The developers of this app clearly do not use their own software in the real world. If you use white noise apps, ambient loops, or background music to block out distractions while you work or study, do not touch the text-to-speech audio button in this app.

Instead of routing the voice playback through the standard iOS media channel, the app initializes an aggressive Text-to-Speech engine call that mimics an incoming phone call or emergency alarm. The second you tap it, Apple’s audio architecture forcefully hijacks your hardware, executes audio ducking, and completely freezes the data thread of any other app running in your background.

Worse yet, it refuses to release the audio channel cleanly when the voice stops speaking. Your background audio stays permanently locked in purgatory until you manually force-close your other apps and restart them. It is incredibly frustrating, poorly optimized, and completely ruins the multi-tasking capability of an iPhone.

Fix your audio session categories. Until then, it is completely unusable for anyone who values their focus or their workflow.

title: the worst AI ever
content: While AI assistants are incredibly useful tools, they still suffer from a few frustrating limitations that can ruin the user experience. First, AI models frequently engage in "hallucination"—meaning they often skip thorough information retrieval, misinterpret details, or make up incorrect answers with total confidence. You constantly have to double-check their facts to avoid relying on fake information. Second, AI systems lack persistent memory across distinct sessions. The moment you open a new chat tab, the AI completely forgets your previous context, forcing you to re-explain the entire background from scratch. Until AI models improve their factual accuracy and seamless memory retention, users must remain cautious and prepare to repeat themselves often.

title: Surprisingly Powerful (When You Know What You’re Doing)
content:
Google Gemini is fast, clean, and genuinely useful once you stop treating it like a toy and start treating it like a tool. Great for brainstorming, coding help, writing, and organizing chaotic thoughts into something usable.

It does take some time to understand how to chat and talk with Gemini to get its full capacity every time and once you do it responds quickly, handles complex prompts well, and integrates nicely with Google’s ecosystem. Not perfect (no AI is, relax), but solid enough to be part of a real workflow.

If you actually know how to prompt and aren’t just asking “write me a poem,” this thing can seriously boost productivity and creativity.

Easy 5 stars.

content: Gemini has some very specific strengths and weaknesses compared to other AI models. Strengths: user interface and messaging tone are excellent (emotionally detached and very matter of fact), high usage limits, and reliable responses. There are some notable weaknesses: very limited ability to reference information in other chats and ability to update and make changes to pictures that have already been created is severely limited (editing text size, positioning, etc.), it makes lots of mistakes editing pictures, and can be incredibly frustrating to use for graphics.

The tech world will not leave well enough alone. For average users these “improvements” are a pain in the butt!

title: Good but not great
content:
I tend to use Gemini as my general go-to AI research tool. If I’m trying to get something to work, it can be very helpful by giving me what I need quickly.  I also use it to help me understand how YouTube works since I’m a content creator and Google owns both. I’ve had it review transcripts of my videos before publishing, but after several months felt that it wasn’t helping me in the way I need. ChatGPT is better for that.

Gemini is great at helping me manipulate images and saves me time in my image editor where the same type of manipulation can be quite difficult.

I like how if I’m trying to find restaurants or grocery stores in other countries, it can do that outside of maps, and then propose a route for me.

Like all AI’s, it can be wrong or suggest truly bizarre things, like bus routes that don’t exist, or be overly agreeable with me.

It seems less thoughtful than ChatGPT, in my experience. But it’s good and good for general research. Nothing too difficult.
